original_text: [TITLE: Мешканців Франкфурта розбудили загадкові вибухи | LEDE: ] (uk: Мешканців Франкфурта розбудили загадкові вибухи) —

‘It Is a Pity’: China Could Stop the War but Leans Toward Russia, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky said China is politically closer to Russia than Ukraine and has failed to use its influence over Moscow to help end the war. In an NHK interview, he also proposed a Drone Deal with Japan and warned that 30,000–50,000 North Korean troops have gained real combat and drone-warfare experience in Russia, posing a wider threat to Pacific security.

Belarus Reactivates Relays Helping Russian Drones Strike Deeper Into Ukraine, Kyiv Says — Belarus has reactivated signal relays that help Russian Shahed and Gerbera drones penetrate deeper into Ukraine, Kyiv says. Ukrainian officials linked the equipment to a Sept. 13 attack near the Yahodyn border crossing with Poland and warned that Belarus is again aiding Russia’s drone campaign.

Ukraine Suffers More Civilian Deaths in 8 Months of 2026 Than All of 2025 – UN — The UN said August saw at least 372 civilians killed and 2,349 injured in Ukraine, with the total number of casualties in the first eight months of 2026 surpassing all those of 2025. The report attributed 47 percent of civilian casualties to drone and ballistic missile strikes, with the majority occurring in cities far from the front, including Kyiv, which suffered the highest toll.

6 Russian Aircraft Hit as Ukraine Strikes Deep Inside Russia — Ukraine’s SBU hit one An-12 plane, two An-26 aircraft, and three unspecified helicopters at a Russian military airfield. A separate joint operation targeted the Yaroslavl refinery, while the president also reported unspecified “good results” in the Black Sea.

Russia Employs 25,000 North Koreans in Drone Production — Up to 25,000 North Korean citizens are working in Russia to manufacture Iranian-designed drones for the war against Ukraine, in violation of UN sanctions. This is according to a report by the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT), cited by Bloomberg and South Korea’s SBS News on Thursday, Sept. 17.

Zelensky Names Anton Kovalsky Acting Prosecutor General — President Volodymyr Zelensky appointed 42-year-old Anton Kovalsky acting prosecutor general, two days after parliament backed Ruslan Kravchenko’s dismissal. Kovalsky, previously the Khmelnytskyi regional prosecutor, inherits an office shaken by an alleged call center protection scheme and a bitter confrontation with Ukraine’s independent anti-corruption agencies that has raised concerns about the country’s reform record.

FSB Accuses Sevastopol Man of Supplying Weapons to Ukraine — The FSB Public Relations Center reported on Thursday that it had arrested a resident of Sevastopol who had organized the smuggling of weapons into the combat zone in Ukraine, on behalf of the SBU.

Russian Drone Hits Kharkiv Mall, Woman Needs Medical Aid — A Russian drone struck a shopping center in Kharkiv’s Osnovianskyi district on Thursday, regional authorities said. A 65-year-old employee who sheltered during the attack later became unwell and sought medical assistance. Officials reported no direct injuries from the impact, while emergency crews continued working at the scene.

Zelensky Hails ‘Powerful’ US Sanctions Bill After Overnight Russian Missile, Drone Attack — Zelensky welcomed the US House’s passage of a sweeping Russia sanctions bill after an overnight Russian attack injured civilians and damaged infrastructure in eight Ukrainian regions. The bill gives Trump expanded sanctions powers and authority to impose tariffs of up to 100%.

Ukraine Hits Russian Airfield, Major Oil Refinery in Massive Overnight Drone Attack — Ukraine’s SBU confirmed strikes on a Russian military airfield in Rostov-on-Don and the Slavneft-YANOS refinery in Yaroslavl. The SBU said three aircraft and three helicopters were hit at the airfield, while a fire broke out at the refinery.

Associate Membership – Appreciated in Canada; a Non-Starter in Ukraine? — The EU’s proposed “associate membership” for Canada could create a new model for closer integration without full accession. But Ukraine, which has sought EU membership and stronger security guarantees, views such an arrangement as insufficient compared with full integration.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 16, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 16, 2026.

After 25 Freed in Belarus, Tsikhanouskaya Says Hundreds Still Remain Behind Bars — With the welcomed release of 25 political prisoners, Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya reminded the world that negotiations must continue until all those jailed for political reasons are free.

US House Passes Sweeping Russia Sanctions Bill, Sends It to Trump — The House passed a major Russia sanctions package aimed at cutting the financial networks sustaining Moscow’s war against Ukraine and increasing pressure on Putin.

Russian Strike Hits 19-Story Odesa Apartment Block, Injures 7 Including Child — A Russian strike on Odesa injured seven people, including a three-year-old child, and damaged a 19-story apartment block and nearby homes.

Russian Attack on Kyiv Injures 20, Including 2 Children, Hits Water Infrastructure — A Russian missile and drone attack injured 20 people in Kyiv, including two children, and damaged homes, offices and warehouses across the capital.

Zelensky’s Former Comedy Studio Hit in Russian Strike – It’s the Symbolism Moscow Is After — A Russian strike destroyed decades of Kvartal 95 history, turning Zelensky’s former studio into a symbol of how Moscow reaches for symbolism when it cannot defeat Ukraine on the battlefield.

Ukrainian Parliament Passes Key First-Reading Reforms for Parcel Tax and Small Business Bankruptcy — On Sept. 16, the Verkhovna Rada approved two key draft bills in their first readings to meet international commitments under IMF and EU programs. Lawmakers backed No. 16051-1 to end VAT exemptions on international parcels under €150 ($170), expected to generate Hr.10 billion ($224 million) annually. Parliament also approved No. 15024 to simplify insolvency procedures for small businesses, unlocki

Russian Strike Destroys Zelensky’s Former TV Studio Warehouse — A Russian drone strike destroyed a Kyiv warehouse used by Studio “Kvartal 95” on Wednesday, Sept. 16, the production company co-founded by President Volodymyr Zelensky. The studio said no employees were injured, but sets, costumes and other props accumulated over 20 years were lost.

Zelensky Signs Law Targeting Scam Call Centers — President Volodymyr Zelensky said he signed legislation creating criminal liability for organized scam call centers after Ukraine’s parliament, the Verkhovna Rada, approved the measure earlier on Wednesday, Sept. 16. The new law provides prison terms of up to 12 years and forms part of broader legal reforms Ukraine is advancing while seeking closer European integration.

Germany to Deploy Eurofighters to Latvia Ahead of its Elections Amid Drone Incursions Risks — Germany pledged to send four Eurofighter jets to Latvia, reinforcing NATO’s air policing ahead of the country’s Oct. 3 parliamentary election. According to Politico on Wednesday, Sept. 16, Latvia requested additional allied support after several foreign drones violated its airspace in 2026 alone.

Ukraine Plans War-Risk Insurance Fund, Considers 1% VAT Increase to Cover Business Losses — Ukraine is seeking to establish a first-loss fund to expand war-risk insurance for businesses, with a 1% VAT increase discussed as one possible source of Ukraine’s contribution. The country also wants to attract at least $1 billion, and potentially $2-3 billion from international partners. Business leaders at an EBA conference supported the need for a functioning insurance mechanism but raised concerns ab

Lithuania Says Downed Drone Was Russian Gerbera — Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda said a Russian Gerbera drone entered the country’s airspace from Belarus on Tuesday, Sept. 15, carrying an explosive device. The drone likely went off course while en route to Ukraine, before NATO fighter jets shot it down.

Russia Fails to Uphold Oleshky Evacuation Deal, Human Rights Commissioner Says — Ukraine’s human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said on Wednesday, Sept. 16 that Russia has yet to approve an agreed humanitarian evacuation from occupied Oleshky in the Kherson region. More than 6,000 civilians, including around 200 children, may remain in the frontline area, with hundreds requiring urgent assistance to leave safely. “The city has been turned into a death trap,” Lubinets said.

Russian Strikes Kill 6, Wound At Least 17 Across Ukraine — Russian strikes killed at least six people and injured at least 17 others across four Ukrainian regions on Wednesday, Sept. 16. The deadliest strike hit a passenger bus in Nikopol, while guided aerial bombs (KABs) and drone attacks caused damage across Kyiv, Odesa and Sumy.

Russia Rewards Captain Who Fired Flares at Danish Helicopter — Russian Defense Minister Andrei Belousov awarded the commander of the corvette Soobrazitelny after the vessel fired two signal flares toward a Danish military helicopter in international waters. Moscow portrayed the incident as the prevention of a Danish “provocation,” while Copenhagen said the helicopter was conducting routine surveillance and one flare narrowly missed it.

“Kyiv of Mine”: American Filmmaker D.W. Phillips on Documenting Ukraine’s Decade of Resilience — In this interview, Stash Luczkiw sits down with D.W. Phillips — an American filmmaker, attorney, philanthropist, and Kyiv Post contributor.

Frozen Russian Assets Will Not Return to Moscow, Sikorsky Says — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorsky said Russian state assets frozen in Europe will not be returned to Moscow. Instead, they should rather be used for Ukraine’s reconstruction or the strengthening of Europe’s own defense capabilities, as deterrence remains essential even after the war in Ukraine ends.

Russia’s Lavrov Threatens Europe With a ‘Very Short’ War — Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said a war would be “very short” if Europe attacked Russia. He also warned that Moscow would regard the deployment of foreign troops in Ukraine as a declaration of war.

Ukraine Bumps Average Salary Forecast to $770 in 2027 – Are Ukrainians Getting Richer? — Ukraine’s new 2027 draft budget has placed the average salary estimate at Hr.34,409 ($770) per month, with previous estimates largely in line with subsequently documented averages. The government noted the figure is relatively conservative, based on the predictions that Russia’s invasion would continue, with a lack of skilled workers continuing to push up the average alongside inflation.

Ukraine to Add 12-Year Prison Term for Scam Call Centers — Parliament voted on Wednesday to add a new article to Ukraine’s Criminal Code to prosecute those involved in operating scam call centers, with a maximum prison term of 12 years. The decision came after an anti-corruption raid uncovered an alleged protection scheme operated by officials in the Prosecutor General’s Office and eventually led to the prosecutor general’s own ouster.

Kosovo Ex-President Thaci Gets Jailed 25 Years for War Crimes — Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci has been sentenced to 25 years in prison for war crimes committed during the 1998-1999 conflict with Serbia. On Wednesday, judges held him responsible for crimes involving 96 killings, 303 cases of torture, and the arbitrary detention of 385 people, while acquitting him of crimes against humanity.

All of Europe Is Now Threatened by Russia’s Actions — Trump has called for a Russia-Ukraine truce on energy infrastructure strikes, but Kyiv Post Editor-in-Chief Bohdan Nahaylo tells World Talks that Ukraine is ready while Russia shows no such willingness. Nahaylo details Russia’s continued attacks on warehouses, railways, and passenger trains, argues genuine peace talks are impossible under Putin’s current stance, and notes Ukraine won’t cede eastern territory to reach a settlement.

Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Plant Faces Falling Water Levels, Blackout Risk, Ukraine Says — All six reactors at the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant remain in cold shutdown and produce no electricity. Ukrainian intelligence says the facility lost external power three times in August and would require about 150 metric tons of diesel fuel daily during a prolonged blackout.

US to Lift Sanctions on 2 Belarus Firms Amid Prisoner Deal — Belarus has agreed to release 25 prisoners under an interim deal with Washington, according to US envoy John Coale on Wednesday. In exchange, the US will lift sanctions on Belarusian companies Lakokraska and Bellesbumprom, while negotiations continue over further releases and sanctions relief.

EU-Ukraine Drone Alliance Lays Groundwork for Joint Unmanned Systems Market — The EU-Ukraine Drone Alliance has brought together 18 founding companies to strengthen cooperation on unmanned systems. Its priorities include expanding production, securing supply chains and enabling joint testing, with Ukraine’s battlefield experience positioned as a resource for Europe’s defense industry.

Russia Must List Protected Sites for Energy Truce — Russia must provide a list of energy facilities it wants protected if it is serious about a reciprocal ceasefire, President Zelensky said. Kyiv is prepared to halt attacks if Moscow ends all attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Zelensky stressed that Russian oil and gas exports must be treated as equivalent to Ukraine’s electricity and gas supplies.

Ukrainian Businesses Expect Hryvnia Revenue Growth, Brace for War Through 2027 — Ukraine’s business sector is entering 2027 with cautious optimism. Nearly all surveyed companies are budgeting for another year of war, but planning to maintain investment, expand the use of artificial intelligence, and continue funding social initiatives despite ongoing economic and security challenges.

Kremlin-Favored Russian General Awarded Medal for Fake City Capture Dies in Action — Russian Maj. Gen. Anton Grunis, 46, profiled by Kremlin media as a tactically brilliant Ukraine battle winner, died in a reported Sept. 12 drone strike by Ukraine’s 427th Brigade “Rarog” near Kindrativka. He had claimed (and reported to Putin) the false capture of Kostyantynivka. Other senior Russian generals also died recently.

Hackers Breach Russia’s ‘Invulnerable’ Voting System Ahead of State Duma Elections — The anonymous hacker group, CikLeak, announced that it had infiltrated the infrastructure of the Central Election Commission’s GАS “Elections 2.0: system. News of the leak came just hours after the head of the CEC told a seminar that it was conducting a vulnerability assessment of the system ahead of elections to the State Duma

EU Eyes ‘Associate Membership’ for Canada — The EU is reportedly eyeing Canada to become its first “associate member” despite having no such mechanisms in place within the bloc’s treaties. The announcement came in the wake of high-profile disputes between Ottawa and the White House, though European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen made it clear the plan is “not against anyone else.”

Democrats Launch Probe Into Trump Jr.'s Russian Oligarch Wedding Funding — Reuters said Democrats in Congress are launching a probe into Trump Jr.’s Bahamas wedding, during which Putin-linked oligarch Umar Kremlev paid for the wedding festivities. Multiple members of Congress have voiced concerns over potential conflicts of interest, with Trump Jr. having shared ties with Kremlin-linked figures as early as 2016.

‘Weeks’ Without Power: Partisans Claim Sabotage Hit Russian Missile Components Plant — Atesh says the sabotage attack disrupted power at a Voronezh plant producing electronic components for Russian missiles and air defenses. The group claims the outage lasted weeks and delayed deliveries, while Ukraine said the facility was previously hit in June during a missile strike.

Oleshky Starving: The Human Cost of Territorial Concessions — The US continues to press Kyiv to give Putin land he has been unable to conquer in 12 years. Anyone who has been paying attention knows what horrors come with Russian occupation. So giving territory to Russia is merely inviting more death and degradation.

US Exposes Russian Spy Network Plotting Killings — US prosecutors have charged five alleged members of a Russian intelligence network accused of arranging assassinations in the US and Europe. The group allegedly offered $40,000 to kill a Russian dissident near Washington and plotted attacks on civilian and military infrastructure in European countries supporting Ukraine.

EU Chief Calls for Creation of a ‘European Security Council’ — Ursula von der Leyen proposed a European Security Council and an emergency protocol for EU states to coordinate responses to security crises. She also pledged stronger support for Ukraine, including energy aid and joint development of a missile-defense system.
CARTOON: Ukraine Continues to Hold Firm Despite the Pressure From Both Ends — Serhii Kolyada’s ironic take on the latest international events.

Russian Drone Hits Nikopol Bus, Killing 5, Injuring 7 — A Russian drone struck a passenger bus in Ukraine’s Nikopol district on Wednesday morning, killing at least five people and injuring seven, regional officials said. The wounded are receiving medical care, while images from the scene show the bus severely damaged by the attack.

4 Years Since the Discovery of the Izyum Mass Graves — Following Ukraine’s liberation of Izyum in September 2022, investigators exhumed 449 bodies from a forest burial site, many bearing signs of torture, execution, or violent death. Researchers at Yale’s Humanitarian Research Lab used satellite imagery to map more than 55,000 square meters of burial-related excavation and Russian military activity. Four years later, Ukrainian prosecutors have identified 15 suspects allegedly involved in the arr

German Drone Maker Goes Underground Amid Suspected Russia Threat — Donaustahl CEO Thumann says he was warned of a planned Russian assassination attempt and has been forced into hiding. Two suspected low-level agents have been arrested, while German authorities investigate the alleged plot.

Russian Forces Target Kyiv-Mykolaiv Passenger Train as 80 Drones Attack Ukraine Overnight — Russian forces attacked a Kyiv-Mykolaiv passenger train on Sept. 16, but passengers and crew were evacuated after an early warning. No injuries were reported, while Russia launched 80 UAVs overnight, hitting seven locations, Ukrainian officials said.

Zelensky Says Putin Wants All of Ukraine, Rejects ‘Win-Win’ Peace Concept — Zelensky says Putin’s objective extends beyond territorial gains, arguing that Russia ultimately wants Ukraine itself. He says Kyiv could accept a no-conditions ceasefire along the current front line, followed by diplomacy and credible security guarantees.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 15, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 15, 2026.

Russian Drone Attack Sparks Warehouse Fire in Kyiv Overnight — A fresh Russian drone attack on Kyiv sparked a warehouse fire in the Sviatoshynskyi district early Sept. 16. No casualties were immediately reported.

Zelensky Plans ‘Difficult and Unpopular’ Measures to Close Ukraine Budget Gap — Zelensky urged parliament to approve seven bills tied to billions in partner funding, warning that difficult measures are necessary to sustain Ukraine’s defense.

Goble: Russia’s Elections Are a ‘Stress Test’ for Putin’s Regime — Russia analyst Paul Goble says the Duma elections will test Vladimir Putin’s control, while Russia’s war on Ukraine continues to expose glaring weaknesses in his political system.

Kallas Calls for Visa Ban on Russia’s Former Combatants — EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Russia is deliberately testing Europe through hybrid attacks and urged stronger sanctions, intelligence cooperation and tighter restrictions on Russian networks operating inside the bloc.

Zelensky Dismisses Prosecutor General Kravchenko After Vote in Parliament — President Volodymyr Zelensky formally dismissed Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko after 317 lawmakers backed his removal amid a corruption probe and an escalating dispute with NABU and SAPO, Ukraine’s anti-corruption agencies.

Ukraine Reports 219 Frontline Clashes as Fighting Intensifies Near Pokrovsk — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) reported 219 combat engagements by 10 p.m. local time on Tuesday, Sept. 15, with the heaviest fighting concentrated on the Pokrovsk axis. Russian forces reportedly launched 68 airstrikes, dropped 249 guided aerial bombs (KABs) and deployed 4,153 loitering munitions.

Zelensky Says Russia Targeted His Plane Twice in Recent Weeks — In an exclusive interview with CBS News on Tuesday, Sept. 15, President Volodymyr Zelensky said that Russia targeted his plane twice with drones in recent weeks, including during travel through Moldovan airspace. He also said Moscow may have deliberately targeted a train carrying foreign officials near Ukraine’s border with Poland.

Sybiha Urges Allies for Railway Support Amid Russian Strikes — Ukraine has appealed to allies for locomotives compatible with its 1,520mm rail gauge amid repeated Russian strikes. According to Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha on Tuesday, Sept. 15, more than 500 locomotives have been destroyed or damaged since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022.

Russia Attacks BaDM Pharmaceutical Warehouse, Logistics Sorting Center, Steel Plant, Killing 2 — Russian forces have launched coordinated missile and drone strikes on key Ukrainian industrial and commercial hubs, including an ArcelorMittal steel plant, an Eva retail sorting center, and a BaDM pharmaceutical warehouse. The attacks killed at least two people and damaged infrastructure.

Drone Crash Near Strategic German Airbase – Another Failed Sabotage Attack? — The scale of the search operation at the site of an unidentified drone crash near the Budeswehr’s strategic military airbase indicates possible concern that this may be yet another potential act of sabotage against a NATO facility.

Ukraine Moves Toward Dynamic Electricity Pricing for Smart-Meter Users — Ukraine’s energy regulator has approved draft retail-market rules that would allow smart-meter users to opt for dynamic electricity pricing. The proposal would also require major suppliers to offer the contracts, simplify supplier changes, and broaden access to eligible EU and Energy Community suppliers.

‘We Truly Feel Japan’s Support,’ Chairman of Verkhovna Rada Says as Japan Weighs Joining PURL — Eisuke Mori, Japan’s House of Representatives Speaker, addressed Ukraine’s parliament, the Verkhovna Rada, on Tuesday, Sept. 15, underscoring Tokyo’s political, financial, humanitarian, and reconstruction support for Kyiv as Russia’s full-scale war continues its fifth year.

Netherlands to Allocate €327M for Ukraine’s Recovery Ahead of its 2029 EU Presidency — The Netherlands presented its 2027 foreign-affairs budgets to parliament on Tuesday Sept. 15, announcing an additional €327 million (roughly $377.8 million) for Ukraine’s reconstruction and recovery through 2027-29. The amount is allocated on top of the previous €878 million (approximately $1 billion) already pledged for non-military support.

Ukraine to Boost Protection of Railways, Fuel Stations — Ukraine will strengthen protection for railways, fuel stations and other critical enterprises targeted by Russian strikes, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. The measures include increased electronic warfare procurement, reorganized mobile fire groups and additional air-defense positions. The government is also preparing backup logistics routes combining rail and bus transport in frontline regions.

Sweden May Change Prime Minister, But Support for Ukraine Remains Strong — Sweden’s preliminary election results give the center-left opposition a narrow advantage. A new government would inherit substantial military commitments to Ukraine and support for its European integration, without the sharp divisions over Russia that are seen in Germany and France.
Meet the Irish American with a Ukrainian heart, John Sullivan — “We make a living by what we get, but we make a life by what we give.”

Russian Forces Use Artificial Intelligence to Show Artificial Victory — Russian sources are increasingly using AI-altered videos to exaggerate territorial gains and undermine Ukrainian battlefield successes. ISW identified at least 35 suspected fake videos since June, warning the tactic could expand as AI technology becomes more accessible.

Ukraine Successfully Tests New Interceptor Against Russian Jet Drones, Zelensky Says — Ukraine successfully tested another interceptor designed to counter Russia’s jet-powered attack drones, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Tuesday. The interceptor struck a Shahed target, although engineers must resolve issues with its control system.

Drone Strikes Force Half of Russia’s Top Diesel Refineries to Cut Output — Ukrainian drones are hammering Russia’s oil industry, forcing major refineries offline, squeezing domestic fuel supplies and pushing Moscow to restrict exports — while Trump blames Kyiv for fuel shortages and rising prices.

‘We Would Have Been Living Without War’: Lavrov Claims West Derailed Alaska Deal — Lavrov claimed the Kremlin’s war could have ended a year ago if the United States and Europe had upheld supposed agreements reached at the 2025 Trump-Putin summit in Alaska; no peace agreement was announced after the meeting. Lavrov said Russia would continue military operations even if negotiations resumed.

Kravchenko Out: Ukraine’s Parliament Dismisses Prosecutor General Amid Anti-Corruption Probe — Ukraine’s parliament voted on Tuesday to dismiss Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko, approving a motion submitted by President Volodymyr Zelensky. A total of 317 lawmakers supported the decision. Kravchenko had resigned amid a National Anti-Corruption Bureau investigation known as Operation Carthage, while denying allegations against him.

‘You’re Simply Forced to Sit Within These Four Walls’: Kyiv Residents Living Under Constant Drone Attacks — Since Aug. 27, Kyiv has faced near-continuous Russian drone attacks, disrupting transport, schools, businesses and daily life. Kyiv Post spoke to residents navigating crowded shelters, sleepless nights, disrupted work and difficult choices about whether to stay in the city or leave.

Russia Says Space ‘Must Be Free From Any Weapon’ — Russia and China have condemned the US deployment of on-orbit space weapons, with Moscow calling for the “complete demilitarisation” of space. Washington says the newly deployed systems can be used for both offensive and defensive purposes. The 1967 Outer Space Treaty bans nuclear weapons in space but allows military activity.

Kremlin Calls Trump’s Energy Truce ‘Good Idea’ — Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov described Trump’s proposed energy truce as a “very good idea” on Tuesday. He said the pause could ease pressure on Russia’s fuel market while alleging that Ukrainian forces attempted to strike a Russian energy facility after Trump’s announcement, despite neither side confirming that a formal agreement has been reached.

Drone Attacks in the Ukrainian-Polish Border Region — A Russian drone struck a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train near Ukraine’s border with Poland, though all 206 passengers were evacuated safely. Polish commentators see the attack as evidence that Moscow is increasingly willing to risk casualties involving NATO citizens. They also warn that Russia may be seeking to fuel tensions and weaken European support for Ukraine.

White House Tells Banks to Unsanction Belarus, Trump’s Envoy Says — Trump’s Belarus envoy John Coale reportedly told Minsk during an ongoing visit that the White House is working to unlock frozen funds held by US banks, with Belarus’s Lukashenko naming the release of about $44 million in Citibank as preconditions for further talks. Despite Coale’s role in securing the release of political prisoners, Lukashenko argued no such people exist in his country.

Russian Casualties in 2026 Top 300,000, Ukraine Says — Russia has lost an estimated 301,030 service members killed or wounded since the beginning of 2026, Ukraine’s General Staff said. More than 124,000 of those casualties occurred during June, July and August, while Russia’s estimated personnel losses since the full-scale invasion have reached approximately 1.51 million.

WWII Podcast to Which Putin Should Have Listened — Listeners to the UK-based WWII podcast “We have ways of making you talk” can see that Vladimir Putin, the self-avowed student of history, has ironically failed to identify that his disastrous invasion of Ukraine has repeated many of the same missteps that led to the failure of Operation Barbarossa – Hitler’s 1941 invasion of the USSR.

EXPLAINED: Energy Truce in Ukraine – Third Time’s the Charm? — Trump said Monday that Kyiv and Moscow agreed to an energy truce – Kyiv says yes but only if others can guarantee an actual and lasting truce, while Moscow has stayed quiet. Previous attempts suggest that clear terms are needed to impose an actual ceasefire – and only if the parties are willing to.

‘We Have Something to Say’: Lavrov Says Russia Is Ready to Resume Ukraine Talks — Russia is signaling openness to renewed Ukraine talks, with Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov saying Moscow “has something to say.” Meanwhile, Trump’s claimed energy truce remains unconfirmed, as Kyiv demands reciprocity and Moscow calls the proposal a “good initiative.”

Ukraine Launches ‘Vivaldi’ Counteroffensive in Donetsk as Russian Forces Face Setbacks Near Lyman — Ukraine’s 3rd Army Corps has launched the ‘Vivaldi’ offensive in Donetsk, targeting Russian infiltration tactics. Biletsky reported territorial gains and heavy Russian losses, while Russian milbloggers acknowledge setbacks and OSINT analysts estimate Russia lost 200-240 sq. km (77-93 sq. miles).

54% of Eastern Germans Say Weapons for Ukraine Are Excessive, Poll Finds — Eastern Germany is increasingly skeptical of military support for Ukraine, with 54% of respondents calling Berlin’s weapons deliveries excessive, compared with 39% in the west, a new ARD-Deutschlandtrend poll shows. The findings come as the far-right AfD gains ground in eastern Germany.

‘Warsaw Will Disappear in 2 or 3 Days’: Kremlin Threatens Poland — Kremlin aide Nikolai Patrushev claimed Polish statehood would cease to exist within “two or three days” if Warsaw entered a military conflict with Russia. His remarks followed Sikorski’s warning that NATO’s overwhelming air superiority would allow it to defeat Russia quickly in the event of an attack.

Intel Reveals 19 Russian Missile, Drone Firms Still Outside International Sanctions — Ukraine’s military intelligence agency said 19 companies connected to Russia’s KRET radio-electronics holding remain outside all international sanctions lists. The companies produce components for Iskander and Zircon missiles, military drones, fighter jets, helicopters, and electronic warfare systems.

EXPLAINED: Zelensky’s Headaches Increase as Prosecutor General Flees Ukraine — Prosecutor General Kravchenko, who found himself at the epicenter of a corruption scandal, left Ukraine together with his wife and sent notices of suspicion to the heads of the anti-corruption bodies that were investigating people close to him.

Russian Frigate Fires Flares at Danish Military Helicopter in International Waters — A Russian warship in international waters off the coast of Denmark fired flares at a Danish Air Force Fennec helicopter engaged in routine photographic surveillance of the vessel, according to the Danish Armed Forces Command. No further details of the incident have yet been released.

Putin Resists Energy Truce Announced by Trump — Russian President Vladimir Putin is reluctant to agree to a reciprocal halt in attacks on Ukrainian and Russian energy infrastructure before winter, people familiar with Kremlin thinking told the FT. The report undercuts Donald Trump’s claim that both sides had already accepted a truce, which surprised Kyiv, and came without public guarantees from Moscow.

‘VOICES. An Evening of Premieres’: Kyiv Camerata to Present Music of Memory, Hope and Victory — “VOICES. An Evening of Premieres” will bring together Ukrainian and American music by Nico Muhly, Hanna Havrylets, Victoria Poleva, Volodymyr Zubytskyi, and Zoltan Almashi, moving from memory and loss to hope and victory.

US Midterms: Trump’s 5,000-Dollar-Per-Adult Pledge — Trump’s proposed $5,000 “dividend” for every adult US citizen has drawn criticism across Europe. Newspapers question its financing, warning it could sharply increase US debt and deficits. Commentators also accuse Trump of vote-buying, highlighting inflation and economic costs, while arguing that cash-based politics is increasingly undermining democracy in the US and elsewhere.

Ukraine Strikes Russian Refinery, Drone Plant and Ozon Facility in Massive Overnight Attack — Ukraine launched a major drone and missile attack on Russia, reportedly hitting a Rosneft refinery and other facilities. The strikes came as Moscow and Kyiv resumed talks on an energy ceasefire, though Putin reportedly opposes a deal before winter.

Battle for Belarus — Belarus remains a strategic pressure point in Russia’s war on Ukraine, with Alexander Lukashenko balancing dependence on Moscow against domestic opposition to joining the conflict. Meanwhile, China’s economic and diplomatic support gives Belarus limited room to resist deeper Russian control, as Ukraine views a possible future where Belarus separates from Moscow as essential for good-neighborly relations.

Russian Drones Hit Kyiv Gas Stations, Kill 1 as 200 UAVs Attack Ukraine — Russian forces launched 200 drones at Ukraine overnight, including Shahed-type and jet-powered UAVs. Air defenses downed or suppressed 187, while strikes hit seven locations and two gas stations in Kyiv, killing one and wounding 7.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 14, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 14, 2026.

NATO Jets Shoot Down Drone Over Lithuania — NATO fighter jets destroyed a drone over Lithuania in the latest security incident along the alliance’s eastern flank, while Poland launched preventive aviation operations during renewed Russian attacks on Ukraine.

Zelensky Seeks Reciprocity as US Urges Halt to Strikes on Russian Energy — Zelensky said Ukraine is ready to halt strikes on critical infrastructure if Russia genuinely reciprocates, as the US pushes for restraint and Congress advances tougher sanctions on Moscow.

‘I Will Go Back to Ukraine at the Next Opportunity’ – Dan Fried After Russian Train Strike — Daniel Fried told Kyiv Post that Russia’s strike near the Polish border was designed to intimidate Ukraine’s Western backers, but said it would not deter them from returning to the country.

Kim Jong Un Calls Russia’s War ‘Sacred,’ Pledges Continued Support for Moscow — North Korean leader Kim Jong Un reaffirmed support for Russia’s war against Ukraine in a letter to Vladimir Putin, calling it “sacred” as reports point to possible additional North Korean troop deployments.
